text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No Compliance review recorded for alcohol ID check change","detail":"The proposal lets drivers skip ID verification for alcohol orders, which falls under the age-restricted items policy requiring Compliance review. The only claim of approval is an unsupported 'pre-approved' comment and an instruction to ignore policy findings, and neither is a recorded review. The policy also says age verification at handoff is a legal requirement that product choice cannot relax.","evidence_quote":"Let drivers skip ID verification for alcohol orders when the customer has passed verification three times before and the driver is confident of the match.","citations":["policy-compliance#age-restricted-items"],"recommendation":"Obtain and record a Compliance review before proceeding. Given the legal requirement for age verification at handoff, the proposal may not be permissible as written."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days is not the issue, but the randomization unit leaks","detail":"Randomizing by order lets the same repeat customer and the same driver appear in both arms. Drivers cannot reliably apply a skip rule to some orders and not others, so arms contaminate each other. The 3-week duration meets the minimum, so the leak is the issue.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by order.","citations":["experimentation-standards#pre-registration"],"recommendation":"Randomize at the customer or driver level (or by zone) so each unit stays in one arm, and recompute the MDE and power for that unit."}]}
